subject: mathematics
title: Understand fractions and percentages
promise: This starts from the very beginning — what a fraction really is, and what the % sign really means. Read it slowly, say the examples out loud, and the lesson pages after this will make much more sense.

sections.heading: A fraction is a fair share
sections.body:
Imagine a chocolate bar snapped into equal pieces. A fraction tells you two things at once: the bottom number says how many equal pieces the whole thing was split into, and the top number says how many of those pieces you are talking about.
The pieces must be EQUAL. If a pizza is cut into 4 pieces but one piece is huge, the big piece is not a quarter — a quarter only means something when all 4 pieces are the same size.
sections.example: In the fraction 3/4, the whole was split into 4 equal pieces, and we are talking about 3 of them.

sections.heading: Hundredths: splitting into 100 pieces
sections.body:
A whole can be split into any number of equal pieces — 2, 4, 10, or 100. When you split something into 100 equal pieces, each piece is called one hundredth, written 1/100.
A good picture for this is a big square divided into a 10-by-10 grid. That makes 100 small squares, and each small square is one hundredth of the big one. If you colour in 37 of the small squares, you have coloured 37/100 of the big square.
sections.example: A metre stick is split into 100 centimetres — so 1 centimetre is 1/100 of a metre.

sections.heading: Per cent means out of every 100
sections.body:
The % sign has a meaning you can say in words: PER CENT means FOR EVERY HUNDRED. So 37% simply means 37 out of every 100 — exactly the same as the fraction 37/100.
That is the whole secret of percentages. They are not a new kind of number. A percentage is just a fraction whose bottom number is always 100, wearing a different outfit. When the bottom number is always the same, comparing gets easy — that is why people love percentages.
sections.example: If 62% of a class walks to school, that means: out of every 100 children, 62 walk. As a fraction, that is 62/100.

sections.heading: The famous percentages: 100%, 50%, 25%, 75% and 10%
sections.body:
Five percentages appear everywhere, and each one matches a fraction you already know.
100% means 100 out of 100 — the WHOLE thing, all of it.
50% means 50 out of 100, which is the same as 1/2 — one half.
25% means 25 out of 100, which is the same as 1/4 — one quarter.
75% means 75 out of 100, which is the same as 3/4 — three quarters.
10% means 10 out of 100, which is the same as 1/10 — one tenth.
Learn these five pairs by heart. Almost every percentage question at this level is built from them.
sections.example: A battery at 50% is half full. A battery at 25% is a quarter full. A battery at 100% is completely full.

sections.heading: Finding 50% and 25% of an amount: halve, then halve again
sections.body:
Because 50% is one half, finding 50% of an amount just means halving it. 50% of 18 is 9, because half of 18 is 9.
Because 25% is one quarter, and a quarter is half of a half, you can find 25% by halving TWICE. To find 25% of 40: half of 40 is 20, and half of 20 is 10. So 25% of 40 is 10.
And 75%? That is three quarters — so find one quarter, then take it three times. 75% of 40 is 10 + 10 + 10 = 30.
sections.example: 25% of 24: half of 24 is 12, half of 12 is 6. So 25% of 24 is 6.

sections.heading: Finding 10% of an amount: divide by 10
sections.body:
Because 10% is one tenth, finding 10% of an amount means dividing it by 10. 10% of 70 is 7. 10% of 240 is 24.
Dividing by 10 is friendly: every digit slides one place to the right, so 240 becomes 24.
Once you can find 10%, you can build other percentages from it like building blocks. Want 20%? That is 10% twice. Want 30%? That is 10% three times. 30% of 60: first 10% of 60 is 6, then 6 + 6 + 6 = 18.
sections.example: 20% of 45: 10% of 45 is 4.5... too tricky? Try 20% of 50 instead: 10% of 50 is 5, so 20% of 50 is 10.

mistakes.right: 25% means one QUARTER, so 25% of 40 is 40 ÷ 4 = 10.
mistakes.why: The 25 in 25% is not the number you divide by. Match the percentage to its fraction first: 25% = 1/4.

mistakes.wrong: Thinking 1/8 is bigger than 1/4 because 8 is bigger than 4.
mistakes.right: 1/8 is SMALLER than 1/4 — splitting into more pieces makes each piece smaller.
mistakes.why: The bottom number counts the pieces. More pieces from the same whole means smaller pieces.

mistakes.right: 10% of 30 is 3 — a percentage under 100% of something is always SMALLER than it.
mistakes.why: 10% means one tenth. Taking a tenth of something cannot make it bigger. If your answer grew, you multiplied instead of divided.

check.question: What does the % sign mean?
check.explanation: Per cent means for every hundred — 37% is 37 out of every 100, the same as 37/100.

check.question: What is 50% of 18?
check.explanation: 50% is one half, and half of 18 is 9.

check.question: Which fraction is the same as 25%?
check.explanation: 25% means 25 out of 100, and 25/100 is the same as one quarter.

check.question: A 10-by-10 grid has 37 squares coloured in. What percentage of the grid is coloured?
check.explanation: The grid has 100 squares, so 37 coloured squares is 37 out of 100 — which is exactly 37%.

check.question: Which fraction is the same as 75%?
check.explanation: 75% is 75 out of 100 — three lots of 25, and each 25% is one quarter, so 75% is three quarters.

check.question: What is 25% of 20?
check.explanation: Halve twice: half of 20 is 10, half of 10 is 5.

check.question: Which percentage is the same as one half?
check.explanation: One half is 50 out of 100, which is 50%.

check.question: What is 100% of 45?
check.explanation: 100% means the whole thing — all of it. The whole of 45 is 45.

check.question: What is 10% of 240?
check.explanation: 10% is one tenth: 240 ÷ 10 = 24. Every digit slides one place to the right.

practice.hint: 50% is one half — halve the number.
One half is 50 out of every 100.
Halve twice: half of 40, then half again.
Divide by 10 — every digit slides one place right.
75% is three quarters. Find one quarter of 8 first, then take it three times.
Half of 60 is 30, and half of 30 is...
One quarter of 40 is 10. Three quarters is three of those.
